clauses.reason: Clause 1 closes the departments and agencies named in it, and excuses their employees, only for the day or days it names. The clause says the offices "shall be closed all day on" "Monday, July 3, 1939" and that the covered employees "be excused from duty on that day." The exceptions it lists (employees excluded by department heads for special public reasons, or whose absence would be inconsistent with existing law) narrow who is excused but add no further date. The command is limited by its own terms to those dates, so it ended with the last of them, July 3, 1939, recorded inclusive; the wording gives no "until" date, so no exclusive reading arises. The acting instrument is EO 8183 itself, and no later instrument is needed to end it. The command is not an implementation date: the order orders the closing and the excusal for the named day(s).

Clause 2 directs "This order shall be published in the" Federal Register. That direction was performed when the order was printed in the Federal Register issue whose masthead in the held text reads "Washington, Friday, June 30, 1939" at "4 FR 2699"; the publication date June 30, 1939 is therefore the date the clause was exhausted by performance. The filing line printed after the order is a different, earlier event and is not used as the end.

research_rationale:
EO 8183 (1939-06-28, Franklin D. Roosevelt), "Excusing Federal Employees From Duty on July 3, 1939". Text and identity: the held text is the machine-extracted text layer of the official Federal Register issue PDF (4 FR 2699, PDF pages 1-1; https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-1939-06-30/pdf/FR-1939-06-30.pdf; PDF sha256 ccda4c2815e91078c2edd896f09782b860b204107f796c32e50c2c51b1809476), grade original_representation_unverified, acceptable_as_original true, requires_page_check false; its closing line reads "[No. 8183]" and its heading, date and subject match the register row. I read the whole held text (page images were not inspected; the PDF itself is not held in the repository, only its text layer). The order has two numbered clauses: clause 1 (closing of offices on July 3, 1939 and excusal of employees on that day) and clause 2 (publication in the Federal Register), plus an introductory sentence that commands nothing. Clause 1 expires by its own terms on July 3, 1939. Clause 2 was performed by publication in the Federal Register issue of June 30, 1939. The first-end dates are 1939-07-03 and 1939-06-30, so the whole-order end is 1939-07-03. The packet's later-events search (Federal Register disposition notes of 6938 catalog records from 1937 onward, plus operative sentences in 17521 saved order texts) returned no hit for this order, and the held-text number search found no later order citing it. No held source shows an earlier end.

savings.reason: The order creates no continuing right, status, property or command: its text covers only the closing and excusal on July 3, 1939 and the publication direction. Any pay or leave consequences of the excused day depend on pay and leave statutes, which the order does not state, and they do not keep the order operative after July 3, 1939.
